subject: PayGrid customer impact — cross-region routing + DNS churn causing latency and 5xx surge
messages:
From: Timothy Nguyen <timothy.nguyen@paygrid.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T18:16:00Z
Subject: Sharp latency + 5xx spike since 11/01 22:00 UTC — impacting customers

Hi Stephanie —

We started seeing a big latency increase and a growing 5xx rate hitting our Redwood-backed inference endpoint starting around 22:00 UTC on Nov 1. Latency p50 jumped from ~80ms to 1.2s and 5xxs rose to ~3.5% (previously ~0.1%). This is causing timeouts in the checkout flow for several merchants.

Attached is a HAR and some request traces from our side (request-trace-20261101.har). We tried switching to the dedicated region endpoint but saw the same error profile. Our ops team reports DNS lookups resolving intermittently to different egress IPs and TTLs have been very short (<30s) for your public endpoints.

Can you triage urgently? We need a standup with your oncall and a short mitigation plan (rollback/route change/fallback) — this is P1 for us.

Thanks,
Tim
Timothy Nguyen
Head of Platform Operations | PayGrid

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Date: 2026-11-02T18:25:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Sharp latency + 5xx spike since 11/01 22:00 UTC — impacting customers

Forwarding PayGrid report — they see latency and 5xxs, and report DNS resolving to inconsistent egress IPs and short TTLs.

Priority asks:
- Marcus: check peering/VPC metrics (BGP flaps, peering churn) between us-west and us-east for the last 36 hours; look for NAT conntrack exhaustion and NAT-port reallocation spikes.
- Rafael: validate proxy/firewall logs for 502/504 ratios and queue depth on the outbound proxies serving PayGrid's tenant.
- Please attach any traces/graphs. I pushed PayGrid's HAR to our incident folder.

Customers impacted: PayGrid (critical), multiple merchants on their platform.

Attachments: paygrid_request_traces.zip (I uploaded the HAR + local traces)

-Stephanie

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T18:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sharp latency + 5xx spike — initial triage

Stephanie / team — quick triage notes (first 30m):

- Grafana shows multiple short-lived peering session resets between our us-west transit and one of our backbone partners beginning ~2026-11-01T21:50:00Z and recurring every 4-8 minutes for several hours. Attaching snapshot: grafana-peering-graphs.png
- NAT conntrack counters on the egress clusters serving PayGrid tenants spiked; port reuse caused higher connection resets that manifest as 502/504s when upstream TCP sessions were recycled under load.
- DNS: observed unusually low TTLs for paygrid.redwoodapi.com (authoritative change detected, TTLs 15–25s). Combined with peering churn this amplifies client-side cache-flapping.
- No config deploys on our side during the window.

Immediate mitigations I ran:
1) Increased NAT pool size on affected egress hosts (temporary).
2) Pinned PayGrid traffic to the regional gateway (us-west -> fallback us-east) for sticky session preservation.
3) Opened ticket with backbone partner for BGP session stability.

Next: Rafael to confirm proxy queue depth and whether we saw HTTP keepalive resets before 502 spikes. If proxy shows queuing, we should temporarily route PayGrid through a less-congested proxy pool.

-- Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE — Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T19:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sharp latency + 5xx spike — proxy and firewall findings

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 18:48 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> - NAT conntrack counters on the egress clusters serving PayGrid tenants spiked; port reuse caused higher connection resets that manifest as 502/504s when upstream TCP sessions were recycled under load.
> - DNS: observed unusually low TTLs for paygrid.redwoodapi.com (authoritative change detected, TTLs 15–25s).

Stephanie — additional details from proxy/firewall side:
- Proxy queue depth on proxy-pool-7 briefly exceeded 75% between 21:55–22:40 UTC; average request processing time doubled and we saw ~18% increase in backend connection resets during that window.
- Firewall logs include several thousand ACCEPTs to ephemeral upstream ports that then immediately reset; pattern matches rapid connection churn rather than application errors.
- We found malformed AXFR responses from an upstream DNS resolver cluster (see malformed_dns_logs.txt) — some clients retried against alternative resolvers, which returned different egress IPs and contributed to session rebinds.

Recommended mitigation (short term):
1) Force PayGrid to the dedicated egress pool (already in progress).
2) Temporarily lengthen DNS TTLs on the authoritative zone for paygrid.redwoodapi.com to 300s while we stabilize peering and resolver behavior. Needs DNS team approval.
3) Request PayGrid to increase client-side connection keepalive to reduce new connection churn during resolution windows.

If we do #2 we should coordinate with PayGrid (they asked for a mitigation plan). If we can get DNS change approved I can roll a zone update and monitor 5xx rate.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Networks & Edge Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Timothy Nguyen <timothy.nguyen@paygrid.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:02:00Z
Subject: Incident update & resolution summary — PayGrid latency and 5xx surge (Nov 1–3)

Timothy — thanks again for working with us over the last 48 hours. Summary and next steps: 

What happened (high level):
- Root cause: transient BGP session instability at one of our backbone partners between us-west/us-east on 2026-11-01T21:50Z onward caused intermittent path re-homing. This amplified an existing short-TTL authoritative DNS change for paygrid.redwoodapi.com which caused client-side resolver churn and sessions to rebind to different egress hosts. The combination drove NAT port exhaustion symptoms (conntrack churn) and proxy queueing that manifested as increased latency and 5xxs.

What we did:
- Increased NAT pool size and pinned PayGrid traffic to a stable regional gateway (reduced session rebinds).
- Temporarily increased authoritative DNS TTL for paygrid.redwoodapi.com to 300s (will revert after stabilization).
- Routed PayGrid through a less-congested proxy pool while partner investigates BGP stability.
- Opened an escalated ticket with the backbone partner; they have identified a misconfiguration and are performing a targeted fix.

Outcome:
- 5xx rate returned to baseline (~0.2%) and p50 latency returned to ~95ms by 2026-11-03T08:30Z. We continue to monitor.

Compensation:
- As an immediate gesture we are issuing one week of Dedicated capacity credit to PayGrid (applied to your account). Our finance team will issue a formal credit note.

Next steps:
- Postmortem draft is in the linked folder and attached (postmortem-draft-20261105.md). We will schedule a technical review with your ops + our SREs next week to discuss longer-term mitigations (longer TTL best practices, keepalive guidance, and alternative routing policies).

If you want a short 30-min bridge to walk through the mitigations and traces, we can set that up this morning.

Apologies for the impact — we appreciate your patience and partnership.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
